📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Q4 alone has pushed Bitcoin several years back across multiple market metrics.

In a recent development, bitcoin’s breakdown to $55k last week took its price back to pre-2024 U.S. elections. So, almost every increase in Bitcoin’s value since the election, even the surge to $126k, has therefore been reversed. The selloff has pushed 11.6 million BTC underwater, the highest on record.

And now, this is starting to affect the Bitcoin options market too.

In a recent development, from the data shown below, BTC options traders are turning increasingly bearish. Put option buying has accelerated to levels last witnessed during BTC’s 2022 capitulation.

Likewise, the put-to-call ratio has reached its highest value since 2021. These extreme readings are rare and suggest that traders are increasingly preparing for more downside.

Naturally, this raises the question: What is driving this shift in sentiment?

According to recent reports, from a market psychology perspective, Bitcoin’s [BTC] drop to multi-year lows has put growing pressure on investor profitability. With 11.6 million BTC now underwater, holding through the downturn is becoming a tougher bet, especially in the current macro environment.

Notably, nothing illustrates this better than a recent Glassnode report.

Bitcoin’s falling hashrate has put miner profitability back under pressure.

To date in 2026, MARA Holdings has sold 40,581 BTC at an average price of $74,446, amassing around $3.03 billion. Much of this sale is related to the switch by Bitcoin miners to AI. Yet, the latest figures from Glassnode indicate that there may be further strains on mining.

Sources indicate that bitcoin’s hashrate is at the moment 8% down on where it was last year, the first time there has been a yearly reduction since China banned mining in 2021. However, whereas the 2021 fall was due to regulatory factors, today’s decline is mainly due to price. The bigger concern is the timing. Just 15 months before the next BTC halving occurs, miners are already contending with reduced profit margins.

In short, Bitcoin’s continued hashrate decline reflects the growing stress across the mining sector.

Miners are already seeing reduced profitability. The upcoming halving will reduce miners’ block reward and so may exacerbate this issue. There is therefore a greater risk that miners may “continue” to switch off hardware and sell Bitcoin to maintain cashflow.

So, for now, the falling hashrate, rising underwater supply, and bearish options positioning all suggest that the market is already preparing for a tougher phase.

Bitcoin’s falling hashrate and tighter mining margins raise fresh fears of miner capitulation.

Bearish options positioning and record-high underwater supply suggest investors are bracing for further downside.

COLDCARD bug goes undetected for 5 years despite 15 security reviews: Details

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coinkite, the company behind Bitcoin [BTC] hardware wallet COLDCARD, has revealed that a security vulnerability remained undetected for more than five years, despite at least 15 independent security reviews, including AI-assisted research.
  • According to the 23rd November, 2026 postmortem published by Coinkite, the issue affected certain COLDCARD firmware versions released between 29th March, 2021, and 30th July, 2026.
  • Although the devices continued to generate valid recovery phrases and appeared to function normally, an underlying firmware error meant that the randomness used to create private keys was weaker than intended.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinkite, the company behind Bitcoin [BTC] hardware wallet COLDCARD, has revealed that a security vulnerability remained undetected for more than five years, despite at least 15 independent security reviews, including AI-assisted research.

According to the 23rd November, 2026 postmortem published by Coinkite, the issue affected certain COLDCARD firmware versions released between 29th March, 2021, and 30th July, 2026.

Although the devices continued to generate valid recovery phrases and appeared to function normally, an underlying firmware error meant that the randomness used to create private keys was weaker than intended.

That stated, the matter stemmed from a software integration error that caused certain Coldcard devices to use a weaker pseudo-random number generator instead of the intended hardware-based system.

Industry observers note that this generator produced less unpredictable recovery phrases, making it easier for attackers to guess the private keys and access customers’ Bitcoin. Although the recovery phrases appeared normal and passed some security tests, they did not offer the expected level of protection.

As a result, the vulnerability reportedly resulted in the theft of at least 1,789 BTC, worth approximately $114.7 million at the time. As of 18th November, Coinkite had received around 300 loss-related support tickets linked to 242 customer accounts. However, the actual number of victims could be higher.

That said, vulnerability significantly reduced the difficulty of reconstructing affected wallet seeds. According to Coinkite, the affected seeds had approximately 40 bits of effective entropy on Mk2 and Mk3 devices and 72 bits on Mk4, Mk5, and Q devices.

According to recent reports, this was considerably weaker than the originally intended 128-bit security. This allowed attackers to use offline brute-force searches to reconstruct private keys and gain access to Bitcoin holdings without physically accessing the hardware wallets.

Industry observers note that however, Coinkite did address the concern on 31st July and introduced additional security measures in August. Yet, it is still investigating the incident alongside law enforcement authorities and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

Up until now, the firm has not finalized a compensation plan. Regardless, it has been advised that the affected owners must generate entirely new recovery phrases and transfer their Bitcoin to new wallets.

This is because simply updating the firmware will not secure previously compromised recovery phrases.

All of this coincided with Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warning that artificial intelligence could potentially discover mathematical shortcuts to break the cryptographic systems protecting crypto private keys.

At the same time, crypto security losses surged 55% to $1.18 billion in Q3 2026, up from $763.97 million in Q2, while reported breaches increased from 67 to 107.

In that, compromised suppliers, delayed patches, and unaudited components accounted for 77% of losses, highlighting risks beyond smart contract vulnerabilities. Lastly, smart contract flaws also caused $569.5 million in losses, while access control and operational failures contributed to another $477.6 million.

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Falls as PCE Inflation Comes in Hotter Than Expected.

Heavy ETF outflows, surging put bets, and fragile support leave traders watching whether a deeper slide is just beginning.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 on Wednesday, trading at around $58,220 as concerns about further losses grew ahead of Thanksgiving. The BTC price dropped 2.8% in 24 hours following the release of October inflation data, which demonstrated that price pressures remained elevated according to the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure.

The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that the October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% in October, matching September’s increase.

Recent findings suggest that core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed 0.3% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier. Headline PCE inflation increased 3.8% from a year earlier.

Recent findings suggest that the report also showed that US personal income rose 0.7% in October, while consumer spending increased 0.3%. However, real consumer spending was virtually unchanged, suggesting that higher prices continued to weigh on purchasing power.

Bitcoin price fell to about $55,300 over the weekend before recovering to around $64,400 on Tuesday on renewed stock market optimism after Nvidia reinstated its CEO, Jensen Huang.

Industry observers note that however, the major crypto “acted as the canary in the coal mine”, according to Glassnode: BTC fully gave back the NVIDIA-driven rally within hours while stocks lagged, then came under pressure. Price broke the $62,000–66,000 support zone, retested summer lows, and is struggling to hold around the $60,000 level.

Bitcoin lost nearly 26% of its value over the past 30 days, and the realized losses are the heaviest since the FTX crash in November 2022.

In addition to that, approximately 90% of the tracked leveraged long positions between the previous week’s market price and Bitcoin’s realized price ($53,200) have been liquidated.

It has been revealed that glassnode suggests that much of the selling pressure is coming from the US. Over the past 20 trading days, US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen around $4.3 billion in net outflows, marking one of their biggest periods of withdrawals since launch.

Spot market activity tells a similar story: over the past 30 days, US investors on Coinbase have been net sellers, while buying and selling on Binance have remained relatively balanced.

Glassnode’s latest data demonstrates growing bearishness among Bitcoin options traders, with limited support against sharp price movements around current levels. Between $58K and $64K, options dealers are positioned in a way that could amplify volatility, potentially accelerating a sell-off if prices fall further.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, bearish bets are rising. Traders bought 1.7 put options for every call last week, the highest ratio since June 2022. Similar levels of pessimism appeared near Bitcoin’s 2022 market low, although prices continued falling for several more months.

Glassnode warns that Bitcoin’s current decline may not be over. Bitcoin price remains weaker than traditional equities, US buying demand is lacking, and the market is struggling to hold its summer lows.

Glassnode identifies $60,000 as a key level to watch. A decisive break below it, followed by a close under $58,500, could open the door to a decline towards $53,200.

A recovery above $60,000, supported by renewed spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, would offer stronger evidence that the market is stabilising.

Zcash holders just got a newly introduced revision as the major crypto exchange Gemini has announced support for Shielded Zcash deposits.

It has been revealed that scott Merkel, 'Wolf of All Streets,' shared this enhancement in an X post, highlighting the milestone as the first of its kind for any major exchange. According to Merkel, Gemini now lets customers deposit Zcash (ZEC) to shielded addresses, saying it is the first major exchange with both shielded deposits and withdrawals.

GEMINI NOW LETS CUSTOMERS DEPOSIT ZCASH $ZEC TO SHIELDED ADDRESSES, SAYING IT IS THE FIRST MAJOR EXCHANGE WITH BOTH SHIELDED DEPOSITS AND WITHDRAWALS https://t.co/d9pIFJ6uJM.

Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss shared the milestone in a recent X post, adding that the recent move builds on the launch of shielded Zcash withdrawals on Gemini this summer.

In a recent development, in July 2026, shortly after the Ironwood upgrade was activated, Gemini released support for shielded Zcash withdrawals to the upcoming Ironwood pool, allowing owners to send Zcash from Gemini to their Ironwood deposit address. Ironwood (NU6.3) went live on July 28, 2026, at block height 3,428,143, bringing a new shielded pool for Zcash.

With the recent launch of support for Shielded Zcash deposits, Gemini users can make Shielded Zcash deposits and withdrawals to and from Ironwood, with Winklevoss remarking that the private movement of money was now complete.

Zcash's total shielded supply now sits at around 4.93 million ZEC (around 28.94% of total ZEC supply) as of November 25, 2026.

Sources indicate that november has brought in key updates for the Zcash network. Zcash's NU7 upgrade went live earlier in November 2026, slashing ZEC's target block time to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The fresh 25-second block target lets miners add a batch of transactions to the chain three times as often.

Sources indicate that none of this prints extra ZEC. Each block pays a third as much and halvings come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving.

According to recent reports, days after the NU7 upgrade, the Zcash Foundation followed up with the release of Zebra 7.1.0, which fixed ten security advisories, most of which closed off ways in which another node on the network (a peer) could stop a Zebra node from catching up with the chain or make it run out of memory. It also added sync and memory diagnostics, automatic peer recovery, and clearer errors.
